sentences: Cutoff is a sharp transition from a distribution far from stationarity to one close to it, within a window small relative to the mixing time.
The textbook asks whether families of bounded-degree vertex-transitive expanders necessarily exhibit that behavior.
Expansion provides strong connectivity, and transitivity makes every vertex structurally equivalent.
Those properties help control mixing but do not immediately force its transition window to be narrow.
A positive answer would reveal a common asymptotic profile for a broad class of symmetric random walks, with the walk's laziness or continuous-time convention still needing to match the dated source.
